verses.text: “Isn’t life on earth a stint of hard labor? Aren’t our days like a hired worker’s?
A servant longs for shade, and a hired hand watches for payday.
That’s how I’ve been handed months of misery and nights that wear me out.
When I lie down, I think, ‘When can I get up? When will this night be over?’ I toss and turn till dawn.
My body is covered with worms and clumps of dirt. My skin closes up, then breaks open again.
My days fly faster than a weaver’s shuttle, and they run out without hope.
Remember, my life is just a breath. My eyes won’t see good again.
Those who see me now won’t see me anymore. You’ll look for me, but I’ll be gone.
A cloud fades and disappears. In the same way, whoever goes down to Sheol won’t come back up.
They won’t go home again. Even their own place won’t know them anymore.
“So I’m done keeping quiet. I’ll speak out of the anguish in my spirit. I’ll tell you how bitter I feel inside.
Am I the sea or a sea monster? Is that why you’ve put a guard on me?
When I think, ‘My bed will comfort me. Lying down will ease my pain,’
you scare me with dreams and terrify me with visions.
That’s why I’d choose strangling, even death, over living in this body.
I can’t stand my life. I don’t want to live forever. Leave me alone. My days are barely a breath.
What are human beings that you make so much of them and pay them so much attention?
Why check on them every morning and test them every moment?
How long before you look away and give me enough time to swallow my own spit?
If I’ve sinned, what have I done to you, watcher of humanity? Why make me your target until I’m a burden to myself?
Why won’t you forgive my disobedience and take away my wrong? Soon I’ll lie down in the dust. You’ll search hard for me, but I’ll be gone.”
